source.title: MentorNet: Learning Data-Driven Curriculum for Very Deep Neural Networks on Corrupted Labels
source.authors: Lu Jiang; Zheng-Yuan Zhou; Thomas Leung; Li-Jia Li; Li Fei-Fei

record.file_problem: none; full paper and supplementary material are present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests dropout in a noisy-label ImageNet setting, extending evidence about dropout's effect on held-out performance.
record.gate_note: The paper cites Zhang et al. for random-label memorization; that is not a result of this study. Its controlled-noise and real-world-noise comparisons test a learned curriculum, which is not covered by the listed versions. Table 4 separately reports a dropout-only comparison against NoReg.
record.test_reason: Table 4 directly tests V6 by adding dropout to Inception-ResNet v2 trained on ImageNet with 40% label noise. Additional dropout comparisons appear in the Forgetting baselines.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that learned data-driven curricula improve generalization of deep CNNs trained on controlled and real-world corrupted labels.
record.recipe_differences: The dropout intervention is a direct comparison, but the experiment uses corrupted training labels and an ImageNet Inception-ResNet setting.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported dropout comparison is for ImageNet training data with 40% label noise; the paper does not report a dropout-only comparison in other settings.

fits_no_version.finding: MentorNet improves clean-validation performance over standard training in controlled and real-world label-noise experiments.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Learned sample-weighting curricula can improve generalization when training deep CNNs on corrupted labels.

fits_no_version.finding: Appendix D compares architectures by their error in approximating curriculum weights.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: MentorNet architectures differ in their ability to approximate sample-weighting functions; this does not test convolutional versus fully connected image-classification generalization.

record.problems: The dropout-only comparison is reported for one architecture and one noisy-label setting; uncertainty estimates are not reported for Table 4.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted for the tested V6 comparison. The curriculum comparisons in Tables 2–5 are not mapped to the listed versions; their results are summarized under fits_no_version.

untested.parts: No fully random-label versus natural-label comparison establishing memorization together with chance-level random-label test accuracy. The study's own convergence result concerns partially corrupted labels.
No convolutional versus fully connected image-classification comparison.

No fully connected classifier experiment, very small training-set comparison, controlled demonstration of excessive-dropout underfitting, or joint removal of dropout and weight decay with augmentation.
No removal experiment based on memorization influence.

missing.what: FullModel versus Forgetting dropout comparisons on CIFAR. ResNet-101 uses no dropout by default, so these directly test adding dropout. CIFAR-100 accuracies at noise 0.2/0.4/0.8 are 0.60/0.45/0.08 versus 0.61/0.44/0.16; CIFAR-10 values are 0.82/0.69/0.18 versus 0.78/0.63/0.35. Inception comparisons also test changing dropout: CIFAR-100 0.43/0.38/0.15 versus 0.42/0.37/0.17; CIFAR-10 0.76/0.73/0.42 versus 0.76/0.71/0.44.
FullModel versus Forgetting on noisy ImageNet changes dropout keep probability from 0.8 to 0.2: top-1 accuracy 0.612 versus 0.628 and top-5 0.844 versus 0.845.

WebVision Mini FullModel versus Forgetting reports ILSVRC12 validation top-1 accuracy 0.585 versus 0.562 and top-5 0.818 versus 0.816. This is a dropout-configuration comparison, not a curriculum intervention.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for V6. Table 4 reports no uncertainty. The extraction incorrectly treats all remaining baseline comparisons as curriculum results: Forgetting changes dropout alone. NoReg and FullModel also have different convergence budgets in Appendix E.1; the exact budget for the dropout-only ablation is not specified.

versions.untested_parts: The random-label fit, natural-label generalization, and chance test accuracy comparison are cited from Zhang et al., not tested here.
No width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold.
No comparison of convolutional and fully connected networks.
No adaptive-optimizer versus SGD generalization comparison.

Tests only an Inception-ResNet model trained on ImageNet with 40% label noise. Does not test fully connected classifiers, very small training sets, excessive dropout, or joint removal of dropout and weight decay with augmentation.
No sharpness or other generalization-measure comparison.
No removal of memorized training examples.
